## Coriolis force in the coordinate frame or from a Cartesian rotation vector (`forcing/coriolis`) {#sec-ch09-coriolis}

sources: OUTLINE.md 9.3; src/forcing/coriolis.cpp, src/forcing/forcing.hpp, tests/test_forcing.cpp at the pin

### Summary

The module adds the Coriolis force evaluated at the cell centre from the stage-entry density and velocity. With
`type: 123` the three numbers are the components of $\boldsymbol\Omega$ along $x_1$, $x_2$, $x_3$ and are used as
they are. With `type: xyz`, the default, the numbers are a rotation vector in a fixed Cartesian frame, read as
`omega1` $=\Omega_z$, `omega2` $=\Omega_x$, `omega3` $=\Omega_y$, and projected once, when the module is built,
onto the local basis of every cell. On the gnomonic cubed sphere the force is formed in the local spherical basis
and lowered to the covariant momentum the solver stores. The option `traditional` keeps only the radial component
of $\boldsymbol\Omega$ there, and the shallow-water equation of state turns it on.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Adds the Coriolis force $-2\boldsymbol\Omega\times\rho\mathbf v$ to the momentum;
@eq-ch09-coriolis-force.

**Data.** In: the cell-centre density $\rho$ [$\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$] and velocity $\mathbf v$
[$\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$] of the stage, $\Delta t$, and $\boldsymbol\Omega$ [$\mathrm{s^{-1}}$] from `omega1..3`, used in
the cell frame (`123`) or projected once from a Cartesian vector onto Cartesian, cylindrical, spherical-polar or
gnomonic cells (`xyz`). Out: the three momentum rows of the increment, covariant on the cubed sphere; the energy row is
not touched. Check cases: random orthogonal frames, a $z$ rotation at colatitude 0.7, a two-dimensional `123` case.

**Placement.** Every RK stage, second in the forcing loop (@sec-ch09-framework).

**Activation.** `forcing/coriolis: {type, omega1, omega2, omega3, traditional}`; defaults `xyz`, 0, 0, 0, `false`.
Off unless the key is present.

**Guarantee / limits.** Exact pointwise for the cell-centre state; no work on an orthogonal frame; `123` with
$n_3 = 1$ drops the $x_3$ row; `traditional` acts only on the cubed sphere.

**Evidence.** Tests: on all six cubed-sphere panels the force equals the Cartesian one mapped to the panel,
{{< code tests/test_forcing.cpp forcing.cubed_sphere_coriolis_uses_cartesian_rotation_vector >}} (rtol and atol
$10^{-12}$), with and without `traditional`
({{< code tests/test_forcing.cpp forcing.cubed_sphere_coriolis_supports_traditional_approximation >}}); these ctests
were not run at the pin. The Cartesian, cylindrical and spherical-polar branches have no ctest. Check:
`python3 src/snapy_report/ch09/coriolis_check.py`, output `coriolis_check.out` lines `[C1]`–`[C5]`, re-run at the pin: all PASS, output identical (Python 3.11.13, numpy 2.4.6, sympy 1.14.0).
:::

### Derivation

In a frame rotating at $\boldsymbol\Omega$ the momentum equation gains $-2\boldsymbol\Omega\times \rho\mathbf v$.
With $\mathbf m = \rho\mathbf v$ in an orthonormal frame, one stage adds

$$
\Delta\mathbf m = -2\Delta t\,\boldsymbol\Omega\times\mathbf m ,
$$ {#eq-ch09-coriolis-force}

computed component by component in `CoriolisXYZImpl::forward`
({{< code src/forcing/coriolis.cpp CoriolisXYZImpl::forward >}}) and, for `type: 123`, in `Coriolis123Impl::forward`
({{< code src/forcing/coriolis.cpp Coriolis123Impl::forward >}}). Because $\mathbf m\cdot(\boldsymbol\Omega\times\mathbf m)=0$
the force does no work: the energy row is not touched and needs no term.[^cor-c2]

*Projection onto spherical-polar cells.* A Cartesian vector $(\Omega_x,\Omega_y,\Omega_z)$ has, at colatitude
$\theta$ and azimuth $\varphi$, the components

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Omega_1 &= \sin\theta\cos\varphi\,\Omega_x + \sin\theta\sin\varphi\,\Omega_y + \cos\theta\,\Omega_z, \\
\Omega_2 &= \cos\theta\cos\varphi\,\Omega_x + \cos\theta\sin\varphi\,\Omega_y - \sin\theta\,\Omega_z, \\
\Omega_3 &= -\sin\varphi\,\Omega_x + \cos\varphi\,\Omega_y ,
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch09-coriolis-sph}

the rows of the rotation from the Cartesian to the local $(\hat r,\hat\theta,\hat\varphi)$ basis, implemented as
`omega1`, `omega2`, `omega3` in `CoriolisXYZImpl::reset` ({{< code src/forcing/coriolis.cpp CoriolisXYZImpl::reset >}}).
The rotation preserves $|\boldsymbol\Omega|$, and a rotation about $z$ gives $(\Omega\cos\theta, -\Omega\sin\theta, 0)$.[^cor-c3]
On a Cartesian grid $x_1$ is the vertical, so `omega1` $=\Omega_z$ is the $x_1$ component unchanged
({{< code src/forcing/coriolis.cpp CoriolisXYZImpl::reset >}}).[^cor-c4]

*Cubed sphere.* The panel velocity is contravariant, $v^a$, and the stored momentum covariant, $m_a$. The module
maps $\rho v^a$ to the local spherical basis with the matrix of @sec-ch03, forms @eq-ch09-coriolis-force there
with $\boldsymbol\Omega$ projected the same way, and maps the force to covariant components with
`cs_apply_velocity_transform_` ({{< code src/forcing/coriolis.cpp CoriolisXYZImpl::forward >}}). With `traditional`
the two horizontal components of $\boldsymbol\Omega$ are set to zero, so the force is $-2\Omega_1\hat r\times\mathbf m$,
purely horizontal, and only the two horizontal momentum rows are updated.

*What is exact.* @eq-ch09-coriolis-force is exact at the cell centre for the cell-centre state. The only
discretisation is that the cell average of $\boldsymbol\Omega\times\mathbf m$ is replaced by its centre value, which
is $O(h^2)$ where $\boldsymbol\Omega$ varies across the cell (spherical-polar, cubed sphere) and exact on a Cartesian
grid.

[^cor-c2]: `python3 src/snapy_report/ch09/coriolis_check.py`, output `coriolis_check.out`, line `[C2]`:
    $\max|\mathbf m\cdot\Delta\mathbf m|/(|\boldsymbol\Omega||\mathbf m|^2) = 2.5\times10^{-16}$ over 1000 draws; a
    numpy port of `src/forcing/coriolis.cpp` at the pin, double precision.
[^cor-c3]: Same command, line `[C3]`: largest change of the norm $8.9\times10^{-16}$.
[^cor-c4]: Same command, line `[C4]`.

### Numerical method

@fig-ch09-coriolis-projection shows the projection of @eq-ch09-coriolis-sph for a rotation about $z$. The force is
a pointwise source at the cell centre: no stencil, no ghosts. It runs in every stage, explicit, second in the
forcing loop, after `const-gravity` and before the diffusion module (@sec-ch09-framework). The projected components
are computed once, when the module is built, and stored with `register_buffer`
({{< code src/forcing/coriolis.cpp CoriolisXYZImpl::reset >}}), so they move with the block between devices.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch09-coriolis-projection
#| fig-cap: "Projection of a rotation $\\boldsymbol\\Omega$ about the $z$ axis (blue arrow) onto the local basis of a spherical-polar cell at colatitude $\\theta$ (sky-blue circle). The orange arrow is the radial component $\\Omega\\cos\\theta$ and the bluish-green arrow the colatitude component $-\\Omega\\sin\\theta$, both in $\\mathrm{s^{-1}}$; the azimuthal component is zero."
#| fig-alt: "Half circle with the z axis, a cell centre on the circle, and two arrows from the cell along the radial and colatitude directions, labelled with their components."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch09.fig_coriolis_projection import make_fig
make_fig()
```

: Code map of the Coriolis force. {#tbl-ch09-coriolis-code}

1. `CoriolisOptionsImpl::from_yaml` checks the keys and refuses a type other than `xyz` or `123`
   ({{< code src/forcing/coriolis.cpp CoriolisOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}).
2. `_register_forcings_module` installs `CoriolisXYZ` for `xyz` and `Coriolis123` otherwise
   ({{< code src/hydro/register_forcing_modules.cpp HydroImpl::_register_forcings_module >}}).
3. `CoriolisXYZImpl::reset` projects $\boldsymbol\Omega$ for the grid; any other grid throws
   ({{< code src/forcing/coriolis.cpp CoriolisXYZImpl::reset >}}). On the cubed sphere it also builds the two
   transform matrices and sets `traditional` from the option or the shallow-water equation of state.
4. Each stage, `forward` adds @eq-ch09-coriolis-force ({{< code src/forcing/coriolis.cpp CoriolisXYZImpl::forward >}}).

### Limits

1. **`traditional` acts only on the cubed sphere.** It is read in the gnomonic branch only
   ({{< code src/forcing/coriolis.cpp CoriolisXYZImpl::reset >}}); on Cartesian, cylindrical and spherical-polar
   grids, and with `type: 123`, it is parsed and ignored. Not tested.
2. **`123` in two dimensions** drops the $x_3$ momentum row when $n_3 = 1$ (the test `w.size(1) > 1`,
   {{< code src/forcing/coriolis.cpp Coriolis123Impl::forward >}}), so the force then does work:
   $\mathbf m\cdot\Delta\mathbf m \ne 0$ in general.[^cor-c5] The `xyz` form keeps all three rows.
3. **Axis naming.** In `xyz`, `omega1` is $\Omega_z$, `omega2` $\Omega_x$, `omega3` $\Omega_y$
   ({{< code src/forcing/coriolis.cpp CoriolisXYZImpl::reset >}}). On a Cartesian grid this is the
   $(x_1,x_2,x_3)$ order; on a sphere it is the Cartesian frame whose $z$ is the polar axis.
4. **Cylindrical** has a projection branch, but the coordinate type is not functional (@sec-ch03).
5. **No energy check through the solver** and no convergence test of the cell-centre approximation; not measured.

[^cor-c5]: `python3 src/snapy_report/ch09/coriolis_check.py`, line `[C5]`: the dropped component would have been
    $-0.20$, and $\mathbf m\cdot\Delta\mathbf m = 0.60$ in the two-dimensional case of the check.
